verdict.rationale: A shared address book with per-group access policies is a fair question for a remote-desktop product, so the axis applies. Sill only documents a per-Mac list of paired devices that can be removed. It states there is no account and no server, so there is no shared console, grouping or group-level policy. The local paired-device list is an adjacent control and earns no credit.

support.subject: As an IT admin, machines and users are organized in a shared address book or console with per-group access policies
